{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Baluchistan bear, also called the Pakistan black bear (\"Ursus thibetanus gedrosianus\") is a subspecies of the Asian black bear found in the Baluchistan Mountains of southern Pakistan and Iran.","title":"Baluchistan bear"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It has an unusually thin coat for an Asian black bear, but this is because it is found in a warmer climate than most of the other subspecies, which are found in the much colder Himalayan Mountains.","title":"Baluchistan bear"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" It is also more frugivorous than the other subspecies, and it loves to eat figs and bananas.","title":"Baluchistan bear"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Haida Gwaii black bear (\"Ursus americanus carlottae\") is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.","title":"Ursus americanus carlottae"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The most significant morphological differences are its large size, massive cranium, and large molars.","title":"Ursus americanus carlottae"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" This subspecies is endemic to the Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and is considered a \"keystone species\" because of the bears transportation of salmon remains into surrounding forests of Haida Gwaii.","title":"Ursus americanus carlottae"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"What is the genus and species of the bear in which the Florida black bear is a subspecies of?"}
